candidates.source_summary: Plans for a direct rail link between Rochdale and London have hit the buffers again.
candidates.source_title: New bid for extra trains from Rochdale to London is refused - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to improve the rail link between Rochdale and London have hit the buffers again. Today, the Office of Rail and Road announced it had rejected proposals for new train services which would have seen Lumo operate up to four additional return Rochdale-to-Euston services on weekdays and Saturdays and three services on Sundays . Among those backing calls for the extra services was Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, who called Lumo’s bid to restore six daily direct services between Rochdale and the capital a “game-changing opportunity” for the borough and the wider North West. But the ORR rejected the plans after its assessment found adding more trains to the West Coast Main Line — which also included services to Blackpool and Wrexham — would likely increase delays and cancelled trains for passengers. It said its assessment following detailed and extensive analysis is that the capacity and performance of the southern section of the West Coast Main Line has not materially changed since it rejected a similar application by Lumo last year. An external review commissioned by ORR also supported this conclusion. READ MORE: Police target crime gang’s ‘spider web of criminality’ The ORR said gaps in the current timetable need to provide important space for trains to recover when disruption occurs, minimising delays to passengers.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Extra rail services could still come to Rochdale after plans for four additional daily direct trains to the capital were derailed. On Thursday, the Office of Rail and Road announced it had rejected proposals for new train services which would have seen Lumo operate up to four additional return Rochdale-to-Euston services on weekdays and Saturdays and three services on Sundays. The ORR said the extra services would lead to increased delays and cancellations. Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, who has championed the extra service, said: “I am deeply disappointed that the ORR has rejected the proposal for a direct Rochdale-to-London service. “I know how much this would have meant to people in Rochdale and the wider borough, and I remain committed to improving our connections with both Manchester and London.” But Mr Waugh said that the ORR’s rejection of the latest proposal wasn’t the end of the line for better services for Rochdale. READ MORE: New bid for extra trains from Rochdale to London is refused He said: “There are reasons to be hopeful about the future. The Bee Network is bringing greater integration of local rail services across Greater Manchester from 2028 onwards, while the Government is progressing Northern Powerhouse Rail and has set out its long-term intention to develop a new rail connection between Birmingham and Manchester to increase capacity on the West Coast Main Line.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: New advanced manufacturing hub set to add £107m to regional economy Major milestone for Atom Valley as Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre base build completes A major milestone has been reached for Atom Valley with completion of the base build of the Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) at Kingsway Business Park in Rochdale, which is set to become a nationally significant gateway driving the development of the advanced materials and manufacturing cluster in the region. The 30,000 sq. ft centre is the first major physical development within the Atom Valley Innovation District (AVID), a 25-acre hub for advanced materials and manufacturing in Rochdale, bringing together businesses, researchers, investors and innovation partners in one location. AVID provides an environment where organisations can innovate, grow and commercialise new technologies, strengthening Greater Manchester’s position as a leading centre for advanced materials and manufacturing. Completion of the building represents a major milestone for years of partnership working between Rochdale Development Agency (RDA), Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), The University of Manchester and wider innovation partners. RDA has led the physical development of the SMMC, working with partners to secure investment and position advanced materials and manufacturing as a priority opportunity for Rochdale and Greater Manchester. The next phase will see work move from construction towards specialist fit-out ahead of bringing the centre into operation in 2027.

candidates.source_summary: Changes to the way planning applications are decided across the borough will come into effect later this month.
candidates.source_title: Major changes to planning decisions are on the way - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Changes to the way planning applications are decided across the borough will come into effect later this month. From October 31, all councils must comply with new Government guidance required by the Town and Country Planning (Discharge of Local Planning Authority Functions) (England) Regulations 2026. The aim is for planning officers to determine more applications, allowing planning committees to focus on larger applications and issues. One of the biggest changes is the designation of applications that must be determined by officers and cannot go before the committee. Applications that can be considered by the committee must be referred to it by a nominated councillor and council officer. And applications can no longer be automatically called-in by ward councillors, nor will there be a threshold for the number of objections received that will trigger a committee consideration. On Thursday, Rochdale Council is being asked to adopt the changes. A report to the council said: “The Government’s aim is to provide greater clarity and consistency regarding the role of planning committees in decision-making, so that committees focus on key proposals that matter to an area while more minor and technical decisions are made by planning officers. “Members may continue to engage with the planning process, raise residents’ concerns and submit material planning reasons. A member request will not itself require committee determination, but may be considered by the nominated member and nominated officer.”

candidates.source_summary: Almost six in 10 people across Greater Manchester have kept debt secret from their partner, according to research commissioned by Manchester Credit Union.
candidates.source_title: Almost six in 10 Greater Manchester residents have kept debt from their partner, survey suggests
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Almost six in 10 people across Greater Manchester have kept debt secret from their partner, according to research commissioned by Manchester Credit Union. The Greater Manchester Money Report surveyed 5,008 adults across the region, including Rochdale, Bury and Bolton. The credit union said 59% had kept debt from their partner. Its findings also showed that 67% had some form of debt, while 10% were struggling to repay it. Among those who had kept debt secret, 47% had undisclosed debts of between £1,000 and £20,000. The most common amount was £5,000 to £10,000, reported by 17%. Family and friends were the most common source of help people said they would approach during financial difficulty. They were chosen by 38%, compared with 18% who would turn to a bank. Mandy Wilcock, chief executive of Manchester Credit Union, said “There should be no shame in asking for help with money. Financial pressures can affect anyone, particularly when the cost of everyday essentials continues to strain household budgets.” She called for greater financial education and better signposting to advice. Censuswide carried out the survey between 28 April and 20 May 2026. It covered adults aged 18 and over in all 10 Greater Manchester boroughs, with results weighted by age, gender and borough.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: This week, Mayor of Greater Manchester, Bev Craig, officially opened a new community fire station in Whitefield. The station, which is part of a £65 million investment into GMFRS (Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service), is located on Bury New Road, and is the second new fire station to recently open in Greater Manchester, after crews moved into Stockport Central Community Fire Station in early September. The station contains state-of-the-art facilities, including gym and kitchen areas, as well as bedrooms. The building has been designed to be environmentally friendly, as part of GMFRS’ plans to become carbon neutral by 2038. Bev Craig said: “This brand new facility is really lifting the area. It’ll help contribute to making our streets look nicer, but fundamentally it’s also giving our firefighters who risk their lives every single day top quality, effective and efficient places to do their work in.” She added: “The pressures on the fire service and here across Greater Manchester just grow and grow. They don’t just put fires out anymore. Think about the efforts our fire service have gone to over water safety or the impacts of extreme weather and what we’ve seen with the wildfires over the summer.” Dave Russel, GMFRS’ Chief Fire Officer, said: “The strength of our service is our people, and they need the right facilities to do their jobs well. This new station gives our crews at Whitefield a modern and practical place to work. It will support them as they continue to keep people safe and serve communities across Greater Manchester.” Two more new fire stations in Heywood, Rochdale, and in Whitehill, Stockport, are currently in the planning stages of development. candidates.source_title: Darrell Clarke wants Tranmere to be ‘more clinical’ after Rochdale draw - Wirral Globe
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Manager Darrell Clarke believes Tranmere need an injection of confidence after spurning an array of opportunities in the 1-1 home draw with Rochdale at Prenton Park. Tom Conlon opened the scoring for Rovers before Clarke saw the hosts pegged back in the second half by Dajaune Brown’s strike after missing multiple chances to go two in front. The 48-year-old cut a frustrated figure after the match and said: “We’ve only got ourselves to blame because we have to be more clinical. There were loads of opportunities and we didn’t take them. “What you can’t do is beat them with a stick. We have to give them the confidence that things will come good. “They have to work hard and produce more of those moments in training, but we’re disappointed.” The result marks Tranmere’s sixth draw of the season, and Clarke believes there are no excuses as to why they’re not higher in the table. “We’ve got 12 points in 10 games, and we feel we should be on a lot more,” he added. “But it’s a results business and we can’t feel sorry for ourselves. If we take our chances, it makes games easier because then teams open up a bit more. “Things become tense as we get frustrated, but at the end of the day we have to finish our chances and I’m as disappointed as the supporters right now.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The decision to axe the idea for trains between Rochdale and London Euston is ‘disappointing’, says the town’s MP and rail operator. The idea to have four daily return services between Rochdale and London was rejected by the Office of Rail and Road (ORR). The reason given was that the additional services could ‘increase the risk of delays spreading and making reliability of the network worse for all passengers’. Low-cost rail operator Lumo had hoped to start services by 2028, with the plans receiving the backing of Rochdale MP Paul Waugh. Both shared their disappointment following the announcement. I know how much this would have meant to people in Rochdale and the wider borough, and I remain committed to improving our connections with both Manchester and London. “There are reasons to be hopeful about the future. The Bee Network is bringing greater integration of local rail services across Greater Manchester from 2028 onwards, while the government is progressing Northern Powerhouse Rail and has set out its long-term intention to develop a new rail connection between Birmingham and Manchester to increase capacity on the West Coast Main Line. “These are important investments in our rail network, and I will continue to make the case for Rochdale to benefit from better and more reliable transport links, including to London.” The ORR explained that gaps in the current timetable provide important space for trains to recover when disruption occurs, minimising delays to passengers. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale extended their unbeaten League Two run to five games with a 1-1 draw against Tranmere at Prenton Park. Dajaune Brown’s second-half strike cancelled out Tom Conlon’s early wonder goal to continue Dale’s impressive run of form while Rovers are now winless in their last five after a sixth draw of the season. Conlon gave the hosts the lead on 15 minutes after Rochdale allowed the ball to go out for a Rovers throw-in, and the midfielder capitalised on that error by driving home into the top-left corner from 25 yards. Ince then saw his long-range effort cannon off the underside of the bar as Rovers sought to restore their lead, but Rochdale hung on to pick up another point on the road.

candidates.source_title: Tranmere Rovers Face Rochdale After Contrasting League Two Results - SuaraGarut.ID
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Tranmere Rovers host Rochdale at Prenton Park on Saturday, October 10, 2026, in a League Two fixture between two midtable sides whose recent results have shifted their positions in the standings. Rochdale moved ahead of Tranmere after beating Swindon Town, while the hosts suffered a 4-2 defeat away to Chesterfield. BBC standings data listed Rochdale 11th with 14 points and Tranmere 12th with 12 points.Rochdale's official match preview, however, placed Tranmere on 11 points after nine league matches, highlighting a discrepancy between the published figures. According to Rochdale AFC, Tranmere began the 2026-27 campaign unbeaten across their first five matches, including 2-0 victories over Shrewsbury Town and Oldham Athletic. Five draws in nine league games contributed to their uneven start, with 12 goals scored and 12 conceded.Tranmere's latest loss came against Chesterfield, where Dylan Jones scored in the 59th minute and Jacob Slater added a goal in stoppage time. The match remained level at 1-1 with seven minutes left before Chesterfield scored three unanswered goals, according to Rochdale's preview.Rochdale arrived on a stronger run, having won three consecutive matches. Their most recent result was a 1-0 home victory over Swindon Town, which helped them move above Tranmere in the table. The clubs had already met at Prenton Park in the Carabao Cup on August 1, 2026. That match finished 2-2 before Rochdale won 2-1 on penalties, according to the club's official preview.Across their previous six head-to-head meetings, the sides recorded three draws, two Rochdale victories and one Tranmere win, according to the published match statistics. Their three most recent meetings had all finished level during regulation time. Tranmere manager Darrell Clarke selected a 4-2-3-1 formation for the league fixture, with Harrison Male in goal and Will Vaulks captaining the side. Nathan Smith, George Nevett and Jacob Slater were among the defenders, while Tom Conlon, Thomas Ince, Charlie Whitaker and David Kamara supported striker Dylan Jones.Rochdale also prepared to use a 4-2-3-1 system. Their announced starting lineup included goalkeeper Nils Ramming, defenders Charlie Tasker and Aden Flint, midfielders Harvey Gilmour and Babajide Adeeko, and forwards Dajaune Brown, Kane Taylor and Glenn Middleton. Team availability remained a consideration for the visitors.Rochdale reported that Kane Taylor returned after missing the Swindon match through injury, while the club awaited updates on Jonny Smith, who left the previous game after appearing to sustain an injury, and Devante Rodney, who had missed the previous two matchday squads. Rochdale also listed Ryan East, Ethan Ebanks-Landell, Laurence Maguire, Casey Pettit, Dan Moss and Will Jenkins among their long-term absentees. Meanwhile, former Rochdale academy defender George Nevett had joined Tranmere on loan from Peterborough United and had made three appearances for his new club, according to Rochdale AFC.The match was scheduled for a 3 p.m. UK kickoff at Prenton Park. Rochdale's official preview stated that the game would not be available for live television viewing in the UK because of the 3 p.m. broadcasting blackout, with live audio commentary available through Dale Player from 2:50 p.m.

candidates.source_summary: Eligible children in Bury can access free activities and healthy meals this half term through the council’s expanded Holiday Activities and Food Programme.
candidates.source_title: Free half-term activities and meals offered to eligible children in Bury
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Eligible children in Bury can access free activities and healthy meals this half term through the council’s expanded Holiday Activities and Food Programme. The offer comes after the school holiday food voucher scheme ended following changes to government funding guidance. Bury Council said it has expanded the Holiday Activities and Food Programme, known as HAF, to provide more opportunities across the borough. Funded by the UK Government and co-ordinated by the council, the programme supports children and young people eligible for benefits-related free school meals. Activities include sports, arts and crafts, outdoor activities and wellbeing sessions, alongside healthy meals. Eligible families will automatically receive a HAF voucher through the Holiday Activities App. Parents and carers will receive an email or text message explaining how to access their account and book activities and food provision. The council is encouraging families to check their messages and book early. The separate school holiday food voucher scheme has ended following changes to government guidance on the use of the Crisis and Resilience Fund. Term-time free school meals are unaffected and will continue as normal.

candidates.source_summary: A £13 million expansion at Millwood Primary School has been officially opened, allowing the Bury school to cater for more than 200 primary-aged pupils with special educational needs and disabilities.
candidates.source_title: £13 million Millwood Primary School expansion officially opened in Bury
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A £13 million expansion at Millwood Primary School has been officially opened, allowing the Bury school to cater for more than 200 primary-aged pupils with special educational needs and disabilities. The new wing includes seven classrooms, a multi-use hall, sensory rooms and a rebound room. The project also delivered external play spaces, additional parking and repairs to the school’s roof and existing building. Funding came through Department for Education capital allocations supporting councils to provide school places for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities, known as SEND. Bury Council said the expansion responds to increasing demand for specialist places and will allow more children to attend school closer to home. Councillor Sandra Walmsley, cabinet member for children and young people, officially opened the wing and toured the facilities. She was joined by director of education Ben Dunne and head of service for SEND Wendy Young. Councillor Walmsley said, “This investment represents a major step forward in our commitment to improving SEND provision in Bury. The new wing provides outstanding facilities that will make a real difference to children and young people aged 5-11, giving them access to specialist support and learning environments that help them flourish. “It was a privilege to officially open the new wing and see first-hand the fantastic facilities that have been created. Millwood is an exceptional school, and this expansion will allow even more local families to benefit from the high-quality education, care and support it provides.” More information about the school is available at www.millwoodprimaryschool.co.uk .

candidates.source_summary: Survivors of abuse and exploitation are being offered help to understand their options relating to investigations into allegations they made.
candidates.source_title: New support for survivors of child sexual abuse or exploitation - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Survivors of abuse and exploitation are being offered help to understand their options relating to investigations into allegations they made. IAmReady.org offers victims and survivors specialist advice and guidance depending on their individual needs and requirements, to help them make informed decisions about their cases. Designed in collaboration with victims and survivors of child sexual abuse and exploitation, the new website provides trauma-informed and accessible information in one place. Users are able to move through the website at their own pace, with natural breaks and options to save their progress and return whenever they feel ready. There is also a feature which enables them to leave the website quickly and replace it with a completely unrelated website for privacy. As well as advice, guidance and support, the website also offers victims and survivors the opportunity to request a review of their case, if it was previously closed as a result of a Crown Prosecution Service or local police force decision, either through the Victims’ Right to Review (VRR) or the Child Sexual Abuse Review Panel (CSARP), and also whether it falls within the scope of Operation Beaconport. Set up in November 2025 following the publication of Baroness Casey’s audit of group-based child sexual abuse and exploitation, Operation Beaconport is reviewing hundreds of cases where a decision to take no further action was made between January 1, 2010, and March 31, 2025. READ MORE: Affordable homes plan refused over harm to Green Belt If a victim and survivor wishes to submit information about a case involving group-based offending that was previously closed, this request will be received and reviewed by specially trained officers from Operation Beaconport. Anyone submitting information about a case has the option to receive updates regarding their request.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The decision to axe the idea for trains between Rochdale and London Euston is 'disappointing', says the town's MP and rail operator. The idea to have four daily return services between Rochdale and London was rejected by the Office of Rail and Road (ORR). The reason given was that the additional services could 'increase the risk of delays spreading and making reliability of the network worse for all passengers'. Low-cost rail operator Lumo had hoped to start services by 2028, with the plans receiving the backing of Rochdale MP Paul Waugh. Both shared their disappointment following the announcement. Paul Waugh, Rochdale's MP, said: "I am deeply disappointed that the ORR has rejected the proposal for a direct Rochdale to London service. I know how much this would have meant to people in Rochdale and the wider borough, and I remain committed to improving our connections with both Manchester and London. "There are reasons to be hopeful about the future. The Bee Network is bringing greater integration of local rail services across Greater Manchester from 2028 onwards, while the government is progressing Northern Powerhouse Rail and has set out its long-term intention to develop a new rail connection between Birmingham and Manchester to increase capacity on the West Coast Main Line. "These are important investments in our rail network, and I will continue to make the case for Rochdale to benefit from better and more reliable transport links, including to London." The ORR explained that gaps in the current timetable provide important space for trains to recover when disruption occurs, minimising delays to passengers. The government body concluded that adding more services into these windows would reduce that resilience and increase risk of disruption. The ORR also rejected the application of Wrexham, Shropshire & Midlands Railway Company (WSMR) for four return Wrexham-London Euston services and Avanti West Coast's application for additional Blackpool-Euston services. A spokesperson for FirstGroup , who run the Lumo operation, said: "We are disappointed that the ORR has declined our revised application for new Lumo services between London and Rochdale, and we are considering our next steps. "Following the initial decision, we amended our plans in line with feedback and believe the revised proposal demonstrated strong economic benefits for passengers and communities. "It would have delivered the benefits of competition, including greater choice, lower fares and new opportunities for growth across Manchester and the north west . "Open access services have an important role to play in improving connectivity, attracting more people to rail and supporting economic development, all at no cost to the public purse. "We remain convinced that this route offered a compelling case for investment and long-term benefits for communities, businesses and the wider regional economy." ORR has approved access for Avanti's weekday 19:29 Chester to Euston service to carry passengers until December 2030. This train already runs as a fully crewed empty service so does not add another train to the route, but will benefit passengers, says the ORR. Stephanie Tobyn, ORR's director of strategy, policy and reform, said: "New services, destinations and greater choice can bring real benefits for passengers and communities. candidates.source_title: The Hopwood Hall saga
candidates.source_body_excerpt: When an American filmmaker and Rochdale council signed an agreement over a shared ambition to restore Hopwood Hall, no one could have fathomed the furious saga that unfolded. What started as a harmonious relationship between Hopwood DePree and the local authority ended up with them being on opposite sides of a court room. Mr DePree claims ancestral connections to the Grade-II* listed building in Middleton. His dream was to bring the 1400s stately home back to life. He even roped in the local community to help him do it, apparently spending more than £750,000 on the project. On what he described as a ‘sad day’ in Manchester Civil Justice Centre last week, his dream was crushed. The High Court ruled in favour of the council following a legal battle over whether Mr DePree had the right to buy the estate or not. The saga began in 2017 when Hopwood DePree signed an options agreement with town hall bosses to lead the redevelopment of the hall. Since then he has led a decade-long community effort to do exactly that. The Hollywood man’s vision saw the hall transformed into a wedding and hospitality venue, with a hotel ‘retreat’, gift shop and guided tours all part of the package. His team could regularly be seen working on the hall’s gardens and titivating the interior in the years since. Before Mr DePree came along, the hall had fallen into disrepair and irrelevance. Its last known use was as part of the De La Salle College, which shut down in 1989. During the 1960s and 70s it was said to be the setting for an underground bar and nightclub. It is believed that Ozzy Osbourne’s band Black Sabbath and other iconic performers played there. Since the closure of the college, the hall has been in the possession of Rochdale council.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Simister Island will be shut this weekend as part of a major upgrade for the motorway junction. The M60 will be closed in both directions between junctions 17 and 18 for the completion of gantry removal works that are currently ongoing. Severe congestion and significant delays are expected. Motorists have been warned to plan ahead and either allow extra time for their journeys or avoid the area during the closure. The westbound route will be closed from 10pm on Saturday (October 10) until 6am on Monday (October 12). The eastbound stretch will be closed from 11.59pm on Saturday (October 10) until 6am on Monday (October 12). Two weekends ago the same section of road was closed as National Highways began the removal of overhead gantries. It caused gridlock traffic on the roads around Bury – particularly in Prestwich. National Highways bosses have thanked drivers and local residents for their patience, but said this is a vital bit of infrastructure work. Frances Oliver, National Highways senior project manager, said: “This is a vital scheme for the north west as Simister Island is used by more than 90,000 vehicles every day, and the M62 corridor is a major trade route between the port cities of Liverpool and Hull. “Improvements include upgrading the M60 to five lanes in both directions and constructing a new loop road so fewer drivers will need to use the island. This will create additional capacity, improve traffic flows and reduce congestion.

candidates.source_title: Rochdale manufacturing centre completes base build ahead of planned 2027 opening - Roch Valley Radio
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The base build of a new advanced materials and manufacturing centre at Kingsway Business Park in Rochdale has been completed, with specialist fit-out work to follow before it opens in 2027. The 30,000 sq ft Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre is the first major physical development within the 25-acre Atom Valley Innovation District. It will provide businesses with specialist space, facilities and access to research and technical expertise to help develop products and bring them to market. Rochdale Development Agency has led the building’s development, working with Greater Manchester Combined Authority, the University of Manchester and other partners. Councillor Daniel Meredith, Rochdale Borough Council’s portfolio holder for regeneration and housing, said: “The building completion of the Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre is fantastic news for Rochdale residents. This landmark facility will help create new employment opportunities, support the development of high-value skills and ensure local people can benefit from some of the most exciting advances in modern manufacturing and materials science. “We’ve worked hard to position Rochdale at the forefront of innovation and advanced manufacturing, and the SMMC is a clear example of that ambition becoming reality. It’s a major investment in our future, creating opportunities for local businesses, attracting new employers and helping to build a stronger economy for generations to come.” The building received £15.2 million from the government’s Towns Fund and £5.8 million from the Greater Manchester Investment Zone. A further £16.4 million from the Local Innovation Partnerships Fund will support the next phase of the innovation district. The fund is delivered through UK Research and Innovation.

candidates.source_title: Affordable homes plan refused over harm to Green Belt - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to build 24 affordable homes which would pay homage to a former mill have been refused because of the harm the development would cause to the Green Belt. Franstep Limited and David Gibbons applied to Rochdale Council to build 24 apartments and six houses on land at Waterfold Lane, Heap Bridge, just off the M66 motorway. Following discussions with the council, the plans were amended to build 18 three-bed terraced homes and six one-bed apartments instead of 12 two-bed apartments and six three-bed terraced houses. The site was previously occupied by Water Fold Mill from the mid-1800s which was demolished in the late 1960s to early 1970s when the M66 was being built. The area is designated green belt land, on the edge of Heap Bridge village. The proposed development was intended to reflect Victorian mill workers’ cottages and each home was designated to be affordable housing. The application received 16 objections which raised concerns about additional traffic and access to Waterfold Lane, concerns about flood risk and the impact the proposals would have on the area. A planning officer’s report said the development would cause harm to the Green Belt and it would be “car dependent”.

candidates.source_title: Major milestone for Atom Valley as Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre base build completes
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A major milestone has been reached for Atom Valley with completion of the base build of the Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) at Kingsway Business Park in Rochdale, which is set to become a nationally significant gateway driving the development of the advanced materials and manufacturing cluster in the region. An error occurred while preparing your download The 30,000 sq ft centre is the first major physical development within the Atom Valley Innovation District (AVID), a 25-acre hub for advanced materials and manufacturing in Rochdale, bringing together businesses, researchers, investors and innovation partners in one location. AVID provides an environment where organisations can innovate, grow and commercialise new technologies, strengthening Greater Manchester's position as a leading centre for advanced materials and manufacturing. Completion of the building represents a major milestone for years of partnership working between Rochdale Development Agency (RDA), Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), The University of Manchester and wider innovation partners. RDA has led the physical development of the SMMC, working with partners to secure investment and position advanced materials and manufacturing as a priority opportunity for Rochdale and Greater Manchester. The next phase will see work move from construction towards specialist fit-out ahead of bringing the centre into operation in 2027. The RDA brought together partners from industry, academia and government to establish the Centre of Expertise in Advanced Materials and Sustainability (CEAMS) in 2023. Since then, businesses have been able to connect with a national network of specialist expertise, facilities and innovation support through the CEAMS partners, including The University of Manchester, the Henry Royce Institute, National Physical Laboratory (NPL), CPI and NCC. CEAMS has already supported more than 90 companies, developing new products and processes and demonstrating the value of a more connected innovation ecosystem. The University is the lead delivery partner charged with delivering the innovation ecosystem that will accelerate the growth of the advanced materials and manufacturing cluster already in the region, connecting our research strengths with businesses and national partners to help new ideas develop, scale and reach the market at pace, and attracting over £60 million in private sector investment. The SMMC and wider Atom Valley Innovation District is a crucial part of our commitment to driving innovation-led growth right across Greater Manchester.

candidates.source_summary: An album of iconic music recorded in Rochdale by local artists has already reached millions of listeners on national radio.
candidates.source_title: On record: Rochdale’s new album celebrates town’s music history – Rochdale Borough Council
candidates.source_body_excerpt: An album of iconic music recorded in Rochdale by local artists has already reached millions of listeners on national radio and thousands more on streaming platforms. A single off the record made the UK official charts, alongside a stack of glowing reviews. Launched as part of Rochdale’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture and released on vinyl and digital platforms this summer the album ‘Kenion Street’ featured local acts performing their version of a classic track originally recorded at Cargo or Suite Sixteen studios in Rochdale. Cover artwork for ‘Kenion Street,’ an album of iconic music recorded in Rochdale by local artists. The borough boasts a rich musical legacy, from Gracie Fields to Lisa Stansfield, and more recently The Courteeners. Between 1977- 2001 Rochdale was home to both Suite Sixteen and Cargo Studios on Kenion Street, where trailblazing artists including OMD, The Stone Roses, Happy Mondays, Joy Division, Inspiral Carpets, Autechre, A Certain Ratio, The Fall and many others recorded some of their most memorable work. PoolEra perform Electricity by OMD, another classic track originally recorded in Rochdale. The 11 tracks on ‘Kenion Street’ included PoolEra’s version of Electricity by OMD, Dreams Never End by New Order re-imagined by Medley, and Jennifer Read’s dramatic version of Totally Wired, by The Fall. All the new tracks were recorded and produced at Voltalab Sound Studios, based in the original Cargo/Suite Sixteen building on Kenion Street, by studio founder Jamie Alsop. Radio 6 Music also featured the album, playing Middleton band’s K-Estate's version of Gang of Four’s Damaged Goods. It was also made Track of the Day on Radio X with other tracks played across XS Manchester, Mersey Radio, Phoenix FM and many more, with a combined audience of over 3.5 million.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Police have given an update as a murder investigation continues in Rochdale following the death of a man. He's been n amed locally as 56 year-old John McGarry - with touching tributes to him flooding social media. Police were called to a report of a 'concern for welfare' of a man at a property on Curzon Road in Kirkholt, near Castleton, shortly before 8pm on Wednesday (October 7). Emergency services attended and a man aged in his 50s was sadly pronounced dead at the scene. A man in his 40s was arrested on suspicion of his murder and was taken into custody for questioning. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter GMP, on Thursday, said detectives were working 'at a pace' and that they are 'keeping an open mind' and 'exploring all lines of enquiry' in order to 'establish the full circumstances' surrounding the death. In an update on Friday, a force spokesperson confirmed to the Manchester Evening News the suspect has been released on bail pending further enquiries. No further details have been revealed. McGarry is understood to be a father and a Rochdale AFC supporter. One woman said: "So gutted fly high mate." Another said: "So sad r.i.p John." A third said: "What a horror condolences to the Mcgarry family x" A man said: "One my good friends r.ip pal up the dale shocked" Whilst another said: "Sad news fly high John." A man who said he had known Mr McGarry for over 40 years described him as a 'gentle giant'. He said: "He was a gentle giant, he was a tall lad. We used to go school with him, he was a really, really nice gentleman. "We've grown up around here, everyone knew him and we've been talking about how shocked we are. It's a sad thing." In a statement, Detective Superintendent Richard Hunt from GMP said: "Firstly, our thoughts remain with the family of the man who sadly died, and we have officers assigned to support them through this difficult time. "An investigation is underway and officers are working at pace to establish the circumstances which led to this man’s death." The force said a scene was expected to remain in place for a number of days.

candidates.source_title: RSPCA appeals after French bulldog found dead in Chadderton canal
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The RSPCA is appealing for information after a French bulldog was found dead in a canal near Middleton Road in Chadderton. A dog walker discovered the male dog in the middle of the canal at around 12.20pm on October 5. The RSPCA said what appeared to be a pinky-red lead and matching collar were wrapped around his head and front leg. The charity hopes the description will help identify the dog, which did not have a registered microchip. Animal rescue officer Beth Fazackerley said: “This was an incredibly upsetting incident for the member of the public who made this distressing discovery, and it is heartbreaking that this poor dog was found in such circumstances. “We are keen to establish what happened, and would urge anyone who was in the area around Middleton Road at midday, on October 5, and may have information about what happened, to get in touch.” Anyone with information should call the RSPCA appeals line on 0300 123 8018, quoting incident number 01919098. candidates.source_title: Council urged to call time on rules which stop former pubs reopening - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Councillors are being asked to support plans that could help former pubs open their doors again. When Rochdale Council meets on Thursday, it will consider a motion by Cllr Richard Jackson to end restrictions which prevent former pub buildings being able to sell alcohol or be used as public houses again. The call follows the recent closure of the Wheatsheaf in Littleborough, in the Grade II-listed Roundhouse. The motion reads: “The Wheatsheaf, a pub of significant local heritage occupying the Grade II-listed building known as the Roundhouse, on a site that has been home to a pub since the 18th century, has recently closed, and that there is strong local interest in seeing it preserved and reopened as a pub, including potentially through community ownership. “When pub-owning companies sell former pub buildings, they frequently impose restrictive covenants preventing the future use of the premises for the sale of alcohol or as a public house, and that because such covenants run with the land, they bind every future owner, preventing communities from reopening their local, even where they are willing and able to do so. READ MORE: Nine people charged after day of police action The former Royal Oak pub in Littleborough. Image: Google “This borough has already suffered the consequences of this practice, including in Littleborough itself. The former Royal Oak was lost as a pub and eventually replaced as a shop selling a variety of vapes, DIY equipment and sweets.
